A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The original method and results can be matched to Co-rewarding-I in v2 despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning and test-time-training results, voting-accuracy analyses, ablations and generated examples in its main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments for Co-rewarding-II, additional training datasets, teacher-update ablations and training-dynamics analyses.

M1.justification: The original cross-supervision procedure is retained as Co-rewarding-I. v2 adds Co-rewarding-II, which obtains majority-voted pseudo-labels from the GRPO reference model, updated as an exponential moving average of the policy. This introduces a distinct teacher-based reward-generation procedure, objective and algorithm rather than merely renaming the original method.

E1.justification: Training expands from MATH alone to MATH, DAPO-14k and OpenRS, with reported comparisons in v2 Tables 1, 2, 7 and 8. This tests dependence on different mathematical question collections, including differences in contextual richness discussed in Section 4.2.2. The seven evaluation benchmarks and AMC test-time task are retained.

E2.justification: GT-Reward, Self-Certainty, Entropy and Majority-Voting remain the main comparison methods. v2 additionally evaluates the fixed-teacher control, 'w/o Updating Reference,' against Co-rewarding-II in Table 3 and Figures 6 and 9. This is a limited comparator addition within the teacher analysis.

E3.justification: v2 adds a distinct training configuration for Co-rewarding-II: 300–330 steps and KL coefficient 0.001, versus the retained 170–220 steps and 0.005 for Co-rewarding-I (Table 5). AMC test-time evaluation also adds pass@8/16/32/64 alongside avg@k. These are added protocols; they do not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds teacher-update removal ablations, teacher pseudo-label accuracy traces, reward and response-length analyses, and stability comparisons across training datasets. It extends the original/rephrased-data ablation to Llama and replaces the generation case study. The earlier voting and difficulty analyses remain, redrawn and relocated to Appendix D.6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-training-run estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added pass@k results and training traces do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All 252 numerical entries in v1 Table 1 are retained across v2 Tables 1 and 7, with Co-Reward renamed Co-rewarding-I. v2 adds extensive results for II and the additional training datasets. AMC test-time scores are revised: Qwen2.5-7B Co-Reward/I avg@8 changes from 25.45 to 44.88 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 9). Incomplete test-time configuration details prevent interpreting this as a controlled performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 corrects Equation (4) by multiplying the clipped policy ratio by the advantage, a factor absent in v1. Equations (9)–(11) additionally formalize teacher-supervised advantages and EMA updates. Neither version supplies theorems, proofs or formal guarantees for preventing collapse.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from reasoning through contrastive agreement between question variants to a framework encompassing both data-side analogy and model-side self-distillation. The abstract, introduction and conclusion now emphasize complementary supervision and teacher-based stability across training datasets. Label-free reasoning improvement and occasional superiority to GT rewards remain core claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that Co-rewarding-I collapses on DAPO-14k and proposes contextual richness as an explanation. It adds interpretations involving policy-supervision decoupling, teacher co-evolution and exploration versus exploitation. Conversely, v1 Appendix B's explicit warnings about additional rollout costs and reward hacking beyond pretrained knowledge are omitted.

D1.justification: v2 adds teacher pseudocode and hyperparameters, baseline descriptions, the exact training system prompt, and dataset sizes and roles. Reported hardware changes from four H200 GPUs to four H100-80GB GPUs. The rewriting prompt and generator were already disclosed in v1. v2 omits the earlier balanced 500-problem voting-sample description and the explicit definition of combined voting accuracy.

R1.justification: Research positioning broadens from input-side analogy and latent reasoning to contrastive learning plus teacher-based self-distillation. v2 explicitly connects its design to SimCLR/InfoNCE, BYOL, DINO and Co-teaching, and adds reward-hacking literature. The existing LLM reasoning and reinforcement-learning survey is largely retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, conceptual motivation and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten around the two-instantiation framework. Related work, pseudocode and test-time-training discussion move into reorganized appendices. The earlier broader-impact and dedicated limitations sections disappear. These changes substantially alter the document's narrative and structure.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the framework diagram to contrast single-view supervision with both proposed instantiations, expands performance displays and adds training-dynamics plots. The original main results table is split between the main text and appendix; ablation and test-time tables gain columns and rows. Voting plots are recolored, merged and relocated, alongside a redesigned page template.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence behind the central stability claim. Whereas v1 tests training mainly on MATH, v2 exposes the original method's failure on DAPO-14k and investigates the teacher alternative through update-removal controls and pseudo-label dynamics (Section 4.2.2, Table 3, Figures 3–6). This improves understanding of both mechanism and applicability. Unexplained test-time score revisions and removed cost/sampling disclosures weaken transparency, but the stronger testing of the central claim provides a substantial net improvement.
